statement: (i) Find $\int (x^{2}+1)^{2}\,dx$. (ii) Evaluate $\int_{-1}^{1}(x^{4}-2x^{2}+1)\,dx$ and note it equals the area between $y=(x^{2}-1)^{2}$ and the x-axis. (iii) For $y=4-x^{2}$ on $[-1,1]$, find the area and the mean value of the function. (iv) Show that this mean value lies strictly between the minimum and maximum of $4-x^{2}$ on $[-1,1]$.
hints: Mean value is area divided by the interval length.
